live_unit: GBp (pence), LSE Main Market, IBKR conid 39131980
plan: No entry. The screen ranked SThree on trailing FY25 cheapness that a +93% run off the September-2025 low has already consumed; the stock closed 2026-08-04 at its 52-week high. Revisit only on a give-back to 175-200p combined with evidence the net-fee decline has stopped.
catalyst: FY26 full-year results (Jan-Feb 2027) — the test of whether the cyclical recovery the price has paid for shows up in net fees. Continuous buyback running weekly since 27-Mar-2026 is a live support under the price but is not a thesis.
kill_triggers: Any entry inside 2 weeks of a scheduled print (nowcast-vs-tape rule)
A third consecutive period of falling net fees would confirm structural rather than cyclical impairment and kill the recovery case outright
Buyback suspension would remove the technical bid that has helped drive the 93% move
Evidence that the 15.7% screen FCF yield is receivables release rather than earnings would remove the last support for the composite ranking
edge_explainer: There is no edge here and the honest finding is why. SThree's earnings are 0.33x their own four-year peak and half-year net fees fell 8% as recently as June 2026, yet the shares nearly doubled off the September-2025 low and closed on 2026-08-04 at their 52-week high. That is a multiple re-rating on a falling estimate base, which is the inverse of the pattern this book buys. Working the scenario set backwards from the current price shows the market already assigns roughly 57% odds to the mid-cycle recovery case; our own probability is no higher, so the apparent 33% upside is compensation for cyclical risk rather than mispricing. Two secondary findings are worth keeping: the screen's 15.7% FCF yield is most likely working-capital release from a contracting contractor book, and the working-capital guard failed to fire on it; and SThree sits on the wrong side of AI substitution, which the house's AI-capex-break call does not rescue, because a capex break would depress technology hiring further rather than send clients back to human contractors.
